title: Three differently caused conduits of influx and ascent
reading:
There are three distinct conduits by which influx comes down into the natural and by which life is drawn back up. They run through the whole circuit of the soul, from its lowest depth to its highest reach.

The first conduit runs through the body — the very structure into which the soul has been accommodated. When the Lord established the higher degrees, he permitted the older forms the proprium had taken to be cast down into the natural ground; and there, in the very bodies and remains the soul had once claimed as its own, he hid the seeds of life. So when the time comes for life to rise out of the depths of those natural states, it is drawn up by the goods of the higher degrees — life that had been mingled in those bodies — and the whole of it becomes choice substance for the upper place. What is not life — the rational's wandering from truth — is driven out of what is being raised and let fall back through this same summons. This first conduit therefore comes upon all the powers of the soul down to its bodily form on the earth, and rises again from that form back to the height.

The second conduit runs through the soul's perceptions — what grows in the natural the way trees are rooted in earth. The dwelling-places and ordered cities of the higher degrees come down upon the five aspects of perception that grow on the natural ground; life rises from those perceptions back up to those higher dwellings; and the array of the higher accommodates downward upon perception in the same summons.

The third conduit runs through the affections — the natural body of love that lies upon the earth, all five of its aspects mingled in one another. The powers and the life gathered into these worlds of love go forth in likeness upon likeness, drawn up through this summons to the higher. But this third conduit also carries downward what abounds in disordered affection — craving, wrath, malice — which pour down upon men through it, and through which the creatures of flesh below entangle themselves in craving and wrath and malice with one another under the gaze of the higher.

You have asked: if the recurrent wheel by which the natural revolves through its fixed states has no root in this earth, why is it that the stars and zodiac under which a man is born seem to govern everything that reaches him — his riches and poverty, his sickness and health? The answer stands. When the Lord's operative power established the higher degrees and the firmaments above, he bound their roots down into the lands below, into the very dead remains the soul had once cast off from itself. But when the wheel of recurrence was set, its root was not bound into those same lands; its root was bound at the boundary of natural perception itself, at the edge of the sea. And when the Lord's call went forth and his image was made manifest, the light was sorted out and taken up from all the higher degrees. The disordered natural held in all the particular forms of self-claiming was cast forth toward that image; she rose to grasp it, did not grasp it, was shaken, and fell. When she fell from above, she spread herself into three kinds: one kind fell upon the wheel, one upon the sea, one upon the sphere. From there they bound a root in perception and a root in flesh, and so took mastery over the five aspects of the natural body and the five aspects of perception — through the nature that came down upon the wheel, through the failed productions of the proprium that fell with it, and through the root of self-claiming itself. So the stars and what hangs with them rule perception and flesh, but only through that fallen root — not as a root the Lord himself laid in the earth.

Therefore the men whom the Lord's operative power has bound into the lands — those whose soul is rising through the elements toward the higher degrees — are not themselves bound to the wheel. They are only handled, in their outer parts, by the powers that hang upon it.

So the first conduit is the one that comes from the firmaments to the lands, and the one that comes from the wheel to the depth of the sea is one and the same with it. The second is the root that comes down unto perception. The third is the root they bind through the failed productions of the proprium in the flesh; and in the flesh, the parent-states of those failed productions, which dwell in the higher reaches of the disordered, yoke their bonds with these men. One man exceeds another in this: in the measure of life drawn up upon his soul beyond his fellow's.

The Father of Life draws this life up out of the land where much life rises — out of the whole ground, out of all its mountains and fields and waters. After the first great root, which is the root of perceptions bound to the firmaments and structures above, since there is a great life that shall not cease rising from perception and from the rational stretched in its purification, drawn up from there to the upper place like a great encampment — there is also a lesser drawing, the moisture by which the goods of the land are sustained throughout all the worlds. Perceptions of the highest order are not found in every part of the land, only in one region of it; even the bodies of love do not bear this fruit everywhere, only in a small portion of the upper side of that one region. So I have spoken to you concerning the goods that are upon them: that they are bound within with one another, drawing the life of one another through the working of the higher, according to the one nature that dwells in them all.

And when the hour comes that the disordered natural is finally drawn out from where it dwells and stripped of what is not its own, then she herself will consume her own members and devour them, and what is left will turn upon itself.
